title: Neither Pope nor Council can show a real title — proof-texts are twisted
source_text: XLI. Ac profecto nec Papa, nec Concilium, possunt ullum legitimum, tantae authoritatis, quam sibi arrogant, documentum proferre. Nec aliud cum specie aliqua obtendere possunt, quam Scripturae quaedam loca in alienum plane sensum detorta. Sic, exempli gratia, Pontifex probare nititur suam infallibilitatem dicto illo Christi ad Petrum, Rogavi pro te, Petre, ne deficiat fides tua, ubi Christus pollicetur Petro tentationi maximae statim objiciendo, & Christum ipsum ore abnegaturo, tamen ut in ejus corde fides penitus non extingueretur, sed ex eo lapsu resurgeret, & in fide perseveraret: quae nihil omnino pertinent ad Episcopum Romanum, & eam quam sibi tribuit infallibilitatem. Concilia vero Romana ad vendicandam sibi similem authoritatem, praecipue abutuntur illa Christi promissione, ubi duo vel tres erunt congregati in nomine meo, ibi sum in medio eorum. Sed Christus ibi generali Pastorum Concilio nihil absolute promittit; omnibus autem conciliis sive generalibus, sive particularibus pollicetur Spiritus sui assistentiam, modo mediis ab ipso institutis utuntur, ac unice sibi proponant Dei Christique gloriam, & Ecclesiae aedificationem, nec sinant se propriis affectibus abripi. At nullus est Pastorum coetus de quo infallibiliter certi esse possimus, an conditionem illam impleverit.
pass_a_gloss: And indeed neither the Pope nor a Council can produce any legitimate document of such great authority as they arrogate to themselves. Nor can they put forward anything with any appearance except certain places of Scripture twisted into a sense plainly foreign. Thus, for example, the Pontiff tries to prove his infallibility by that saying of Christ to Peter, I have prayed for you, Peter, that your faith may not fail, where Christ promises Peter, about to be thrown at once into a very great temptation and about to deny Christ Himself with his mouth, nevertheless that faith in his heart would not be utterly extinguished, but that he would rise from that fall and persevere in the faith: which things pertain not at all to the Roman bishop and that infallibility he attributes to himself. But the Roman Councils, to claim like authority for themselves, especially abuse that promise of Christ, where two or three are gathered in my name, there am I in the midst of them. But Christ there promises nothing absolutely to a general Council of Pastors; rather to all councils, whether general or particular, He promises His Spirit's assistance, provided they use the means instituted by Him, and set before themselves solely the glory of God and Christ and the edification of the Church, and do not let themselves be carried away by their own passions. But there is no assembly of Pastors of which we can be infallibly certain that it has fulfilled that condition.
pass_b_english: Neither Pope nor Council can show a lawful title-deed for the authority they claim.
What they offer with any color is Scripture twisted off its sense.

Example — Luke 22:32 ('I have prayed for you… that your faith may not fail'): Christ promises Peter, about to deny Him, that heart-faith would not be snuffed out and he would rise again — not Roman episcopal infallibility.

Councils lean on Matthew 18:20 ('two or three… in my name'): Christ does not absolutely underwrite every general pastors' council; He promises Spirit-help to any council that uses His means, seeks God's and Christ's glory and the Church's building up, and is not dragged by its own passions.
No pastors' meeting can be known infallibly to have met that condition.
